intent: Owner-authorized public presentation of six portfolio concepts and documented work, 2026-10-09. Public placeholders are not case-study or media release approvals.

items.name: Tari Cookies
items.category: Customer Research · UX Design · Digital Experience
items.headline: Designing a clearer ordering journey.
items.description: A collaborative academic UX project exploring how customer research can inform a clearer hampers ordering experience. Design assets and team attribution are still being prepared for publication.

items.name: Hey by Ars
items.headline: One browser. Two modes of control.
items.description: An Android and MCP-based project exploring AI-driven browser actions, shared browser interaction, and explicit human takeover. Implementation and scoped tests are documented, with physical-device validation still in progress.

items.name: waai.id
items.category: Content Strategy · Creative Direction · Audience Insights
items.headline: Stories shaped by human understanding.
items.description: An editorial storytelling initiative connecting audience insights, writing, creative direction, publishing, and performance review. Original video is not reproduced here while cross-site usage is reviewed.

items.name: Personal Browser Operator
items.headline: Automation that verifies its actions.
items.description: A Playwright-based browser operator built around semantic observation, bounded interactions, stale-reference rejection, and postcondition verification, with real Chromium and container tests covering a defined development scope.

items.name: SarafCare
items.category: Campaign Strategy · Meta Ads · Customer Journey
items.headline: From paid attention to real conversations.
items.description: A local-service campaign experiment connecting offer messaging, geographic targeting, and a WhatsApp-led enquiry journey. Campaign materials and reported outcomes are withheld pending verification.

items.name: Motion Render Video
items.headline: Exploring motion through code.
items.description: A code-rendered audiovisual study of form, timing, and movement, supported by an original six-second 2D video, sampled frames, and scoped technical verification.
